paite: Huailouin Elihuin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
Hiai na dikna hiin na ngaihtuah hia, ahihkeileh, keia mawng ahi, Pathian mai ah, na chi hia,
english: “Do you think this to be your right, or do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’

paite: Kei adingin bang phattuamna a om dia? huan. Ka khelh nak sal aleh, bang phattuamna ka neia? na chih?
english: That you ask, ‘What advantage will it be to you? What profit shall I have, more than if I had sinned?’

paite: Nang, leh na kianga na lawmte ka hondawng ding.
english: I will answer you, and your companions with you.

paite: Vante lam en inla, mu in; huan vante, nang sanga sangjaw, en in.
english: Look to the heavens, and see. See the skies, which are higher than you.

paite: Na hihkhelh leh, amah dema bang hih na hia? Huan na tatleknate punsak hileh, amah tunga bang hih na hia?
english: If you have sinned, what effect do you have against him? If your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to him?

paite: Daktat hi lechin, amah bang na pia a? Ahihkeileh na khut akipan bang a mu a?
english: If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?

paite: Na gitlouhnain mi bang bangin a hihna thei a; huan na diktatnain mihing tapa a hih hampha thei hi.
english: Your wickedness may hurt a man as you are, and your righteousness may profit a son of man.

paite: Nuaisiahna tam mahmah jiakin a kikou khia ua; mi hat ban jiakin panpih deihin a kikou uh.
english: “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out. They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.

paite: Himahleh kuamahin, Jan chia late pia, Pathian kei Bawlpa koia om ahia;
english: But none says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,

paite: Leia gamsate sanga honsinsak tamjaw leh, vana vasate sanga hon pilsakjaw? A chi kei uh.
english: who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?’

paite: Huailaiah a kikou ua, himahleh, mi gilou kisaktheihna jiakin, kuamahin dawnna a pe kei uh.
english: There they cry, but none gives answer, because of the pride of evil men.

paite: Chihtaktakin Pathianin bangmahlou aza kei dia, Thil bangkim hihtheiin leng a limsak sak kei ding hi.
english: Surely God will not hear an empty cry, neither will the Almighty regard it.

paite: Nang ngial houh: Amah ka mu kei, a thu maah a om, amah ka ngak hi, na chih vial.
english: How much less when you say you don’t see him. The cause is before him, and you wait for him!

paite: Himahleh tuin, heha a veh louha, kiotsakna leng a limsaklouin jiakin;Huaijiakin Jobin bangmahlouin a kam a ka ahi; theihna beiin thu a tamsak ahi.
english: But now, because he has not visited in his anger, neither does he greatly regard arrogance.

paite: Huaijiakin Jobin bangmahlouin a kam a ka ahi; theihna beiin thu a tamsak ahi.
english: Therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge.”
